text:
Jordan (ACME Customer): Hi, hitting a burst of 502/504s from the hosted API starting ~11:30 UTC. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. curl returns 502 for some requests, 200 for others. sample req-id: r-8a3f2c. Can we triage?
Sam (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste the curl you used and the exact timestamp + req-id? also any customer-side retries?
Jordan (ACME Customer): here's the curl we used (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"rw-45b","input":"hello"}'
```
Occurred ~2026-03-17T11:30:22Z and 11:31:05Z. We do exponential backoff but saw a spike of failed requests. No pattern by payload size.
Sam (Support): thanks — can you add header `x-rw-trace: r-8a3f2c` to a failing curl and paste response headers? also any client IP or region?
Jordan (ACME Customer): client region: us-west-2. added header; response headers:
```
HTTP/2 502
date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:30:22 GMT
content-type: application/json
x-rw-request-id: r-8a3f2c
server: envoy/1.21.1
retry-after: 0
```
Body: `{"error":"upstream read timeout"}`
Sam (Support): Envoy in the edge returning upstream read timeout — forwarding trace to @Ana and @Mike. Ana, any quick checks on h2 conn pools / upstream saturation?
Ana (Eng-SRE): I see a correlated spike in envoy upstream queueing and an increase in `upstream_rq_timeout` for several frontdoors at 11:30 UTC. matching r-8a3f2c in traces. Probable causes: burst of long-lived streams or keepalive pool exhaustion on midproxy. pulling proxy logs now.
Mike (Runtime): Noted — we rolled a model swap around 11:25 UTC to a heavier variant with longer cold startup KV loads. That can increase tail latency on some backends. Also seeing increased `tcp_keepalive` drops on midproxy during that window.
Ana (Eng-SRE): quick repro attempt: large batch embed requests + model swap = higher per-request CPU on dedicated workers -> slower upstream ACK -> Envoy times out. I recommend increasing upstream timeout for a canary, and check midproxy keepalive settings (max concurrent streams per connection).
Sam (Support): Jordan, two quick mitigations: 1) can you enable client-side jittered retry (small backoff) for 502s for the next hour, 2) I'll ask infra to enable a temporary upstream-timeout bump for affected frontdoor.
Jordan (ACME Customer): will enable jittered retries. Are there any headers we should look for to route to fallback model?
Mike (Runtime): you can send `x-model-variant: rw-45b-light` to force a lighter variant if you want a quick fallback. That avoids heavy cold KV.
Ana (Eng-SRE): infra action items: (1) check midproxy keepalive pool — there are log lines like `connection close: stream reset, reason=GOAWAY` around the window, (2) bump envoy `upstream_rq_timeout` from 30s to 45s on the canary for this tenant path, (3) monitor `upstream_rq_pending_overflow`.
InfraBot: deploy request created: DPL-8821 to bump timeout on frontdoor canary.
Sam (Support): created internal ticket SUP-1298 linking the customer's req-id + traces. I'll follow up after canary is live.
Jordan (ACME Customer): thanks — after enabling retries we saw error rate drop ~60% in the last 10m. keep me posted on canary. :thumbsup:
Ana (Eng-SRE): canary is live (DPL-8821) — seeing fewer `upstream_rq_timeout` errors for r-8a3f2c trace set. keeping an eye for 15m. :white_check_mark:
Mike (Runtime): follow-up: we'll evaluate model warmup/kv prefetching to reduce cold tail next release.
Sam (Support): closing temporary loop — I'll update SUP-1298 with timeline and recommended long-term fixes. If errors reappear, ping this thread and we'll escalate.
Jordan (ACME Customer): appreciated, please add any recommended client-side flags.
Sam (Support): recommendation noted: jittered retries, `x-model-variant` fallback, and request-level timeout extension on client if possible.
Jordan (ACME Customer): got it, thanks everyone.
